default.q.n5-type-1-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is (b). でんしゃ.
default.q.n5-type-1-q1-1.explanation: Translation: 'I go to work by train every morning.' / Key pronunciation point: Distinguish the voiced sound (でん) from the voiceless sound (しゃ) in the compound word N5「電車」(でんしゃ).
default.q.n5-type-1-q1-1.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the On-reading of 「電」 (electricity) is 「でん」, with a voiced sound, not 「てん」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q1-1.why.1: (b) Correct because the word「電車」is formed from「電」(でん) and「車」(しゃ), and is correctly read「でんしゃ」, meaning “train.”
default.q.n5-type-1-q1-1.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 車 in this compound is read しゃ, an unvoiced sound, and does not undergo voicing to become じゃ.
default.q.n5-type-1-q1-1.why.3: (d) Incorrect because both sounds are wrong: the initial 「てん」 and the following 「じゃ」 were both misread.
default.q.n5-type-1-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is (a). こんしゅう.
default.q.n5-type-1-q2-2.explanation: Meaning: "I will meet my friends this Sunday." / Key pronunciation point: Remember the long vowel 「う」 in 週「週」(しゅう), and the on-reading 「こん」 of 今 in 「今週」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q2-2.why.0: (a) Correct because 「今」(Kim) combines with 「週」(Chu) to form 「今週」, whose standard on-reading is 「こんしゅう」; 「週」(しゅう) contains the long vowel 「う」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q2-2.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the long vowel う is missing from the second syllable: 「週」must be read 「しゅう」, not the short sound 「しゅ」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q2-2.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the sound「しゅう」has been mistakenly written as the voiced sound「じゅう」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q2-2.why.3: (d) Incorrect because it wrongly combines the kun-reading「いま」of「今」(いま) with the on-reading「しゅう」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is (d). がっこう.
default.q.n5-type-1-q3-3.explanation: Translation: "There is a test at school tomorrow." / Key pronunciation point: The sokuon sound change occurs when「学」(がく) combines with「校」(こう), producing「がっこう」with a long「う」sound at the end.
default.q.n5-type-1-q3-3.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the word requires a geminate consonant (the く of がく combines with the か-row sound and changes to the small っ).
default.q.n5-type-1-q3-3.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 学 begins with the voiced sound「が」, not the unvoiced sound「か」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q3-3.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the long vowel「う」is missing at the end; 「校」is read「こう」, not「こ」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q3-3.why.3: (d) Correct because when 「学」(がく) combines with 「校」(こう), rendaku gemination produces 「がっこう」, meaning "school."
default.q.n5-type-1-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is (c). あたらしい.
default.q.n5-type-1-q4-4.explanation: Translation: "Yesterday, I bought a new book." / Key pronunciation point: Remember the correct kun-reading「あたらしい」of the adjective「新しい」, and do not confuse it with the on-reading「しん」or apply voicing incorrectly.
default.q.n5-type-1-q4-4.why.0: (a) Incorrect because it is confused with the archaic/original form「あらた」(in「あらたな」). The i-adjective for 新 is「あたらしい」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q4-4.why.1: (b) Incorrect because it wrongly combines the on-reading「しん」(as in「新聞」) with the ending「しい」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q4-4.why.2: (c) Correct because the i-adjective 「新しい」has the standard kun-reading 「あたらしい」and means “new.”
default.q.n5-type-1-q4-4.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the sound「し」has been mistakenly written as the voiced sound「じ」(「じい」).
default.q.n5-type-1-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is (b). ひとり.
default.q.n5-type-1-q5-5.explanation: Meaning: "I watched a movie alone yesterday." / Key pronunciation point: The special N5 counters for people are 「ひとり」(一人) for one person and 「ふたり」(二人) for two people; they are not formed with the on-reading 「いちにん」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q5-5.why.0: (a) Incorrect because it mechanically applies the usual on-reading (「一」(いち) +「人」(にん)), whereas counting one person requires a special reading.
default.q.n5-type-1-q5-5.why.1: (b) Correct because 「一人」 is a special case when counting people in Japanese and is read as 「ひとり」, meaning “alone” or “one person.”
default.q.n5-type-1-q5-5.why.2: (c) Incorrect because it combines the on-reading 「いち」 with the on-reading 「じん」, which is used for nationalities such as 「ベトナムじん」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q5-5.why.3: (d) Incorrect because it combines the kun-reading 「ひと」 with the on-reading 「にん」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is (c). のみもの.
default.q.n5-type-1-q6-6.explanation: Translation: There are cold drinks on the table. / The key pronunciation point is the compound pattern verb + noun「～物」(～もの): the kanji for “drink” is read「のみ」and the kanji for “thing” is read「もの」, giving「のみもの」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q6-6.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the first half uses the kun-reading 「のみ」, while the second half uses the on-reading 「ぶつ」 of 「物」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q6-6.why.1: (b) Incorrect because reading the entire word with the on-readings 「いん」＋「ぶつ」 is not the usual reading of the noun for an ordinary beverage.
default.q.n5-type-1-q6-6.why.2: (c) Correct. The compound noun 「飲み物」 combines the continuative form of the verb 「飲む」(のみ) with 「物」(もの). It is correctly read 「のみもの」 and means “beverage, drink.”
default.q.n5-type-1-q6-6.why.3: (d) Incorrect because it uses the shortened, colloquial expression 「もん」instead of the standard vocabulary word 「もの」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is (d). うしろ.
default.q.n5-type-1-q7-7.explanation: Meaning: “There is a schoolbag behind the chair.” / Core pronunciation point: Distinguish the readings of 後: with the okurigana ろ, it is うしろ (behind); by itself, it can be あと (afterward); its on-reading is ご, as in 午後.
default.q.n5-type-1-q7-7.why.0: (a) Incorrect because it is confused with the on-reading ご (as in「午後」) or the suffix「ごろ」(頃), meaning “around.”
default.q.n5-type-1-q7-7.why.1: (b) Incorrect because it confuses another reading of 後, 「あと」(after), and adds 「ろ」to form 「あとろ」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q7-7.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the final vowel「ろ」is mistaken for「る」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q7-7.why.3: (d) Correct, because 「後」 with the okurigana 「ろ」 (後ろ) is correctly read 「うしろ」 and means “behind” or “the rear.”
default.q.n5-type-1-q8-8.explanation: Meaning: "Turn right at the next corner." Key point: the kanji for the direction word 「みぎ」 (right) is 右. Be careful not to confuse it with visually similar kanji such as 「左」 (left), 「友」 (friend), and 「石」 (stone).
default.q.n5-type-1-q8-8.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「左」(LEFT) means “left side” and is read 「ひだり」(hidari). Its lower component is 「工」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q8-8.why.1: (b) Correct because 「右」means “right,” is read 「みぎ」(migi), and contains 「口」in its lower part.
default.q.n5-type-1-q8-8.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「友」 means “friend,” is read 「とも」 (as in ともだち), and its lower part is 「又」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q8-8.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「石」means “stone” and is read 「いし」(ishi); its first stroke is a continuous horizontal stroke 「一」, not a diagonal stroke.
default.q.n5-type-1-q9-9.explanation: Meaning: "There is a mailbox between the bank and the bookstore." Key point: Distinguish among kanji containing the 門 radical to identify 「間」 (あいだ), meaning the space between or in the middle.
default.q.n5-type-1-q9-9.why.0: (a) Correct because 「間」 means “between” or “the interval between,” is read 「あいだ」, and contains the kanji 「日」 inside the 門 radical.
default.q.n5-type-1-q9-9.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 聞 means “to hear” or “listen,” is read 「きく」(kiku), and contains the radical 耳 (“ear”) inside 門.
default.q.n5-type-1-q9-9.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「開」means “to open” and is read 「あける／ひらく」(akeru/hiraku); inside the 門 radical is 「幵」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q9-9.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「問」 means “to ask” or “question” and is read in 「もんだい」 (mondai). The component inside the 門 radical is 口.
default.q.n5-type-1-q10-10.explanation: Meaning: "There is a small bird outside in the yard." Key point: The kanji for the animal 「鳥」 (とり), distinguished from 「魚」 (fish), 「馬」 (horse), and the similarly structured 「島」 (island).
default.q.n5-type-1-q10-10.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「魚」 means “fish” and is read 「さかな」 (sakana).
default.q.n5-type-1-q10-10.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「馬」 means “horse” and is read as 「うま」 (uma).
default.q.n5-type-1-q10-10.why.2: (c) Correct. 「鳥」 means “bird” and is read 「とり」(tori). Its form includes a stroke representing the bird’s eye and four fire-like dots at the tail or feet.
default.q.n5-type-1-q10-10.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「島」 means "island" and is read 「しま」 (shima); it contains the 山 radical.
default.q.n5-type-1-q11-11.explanation: Sentence translation: “Spring has arrived, and beautiful flowers have bloomed.” Key point: The kanji 「花」 (flower - はな) has the grass radical 「艹」 at the top. Distinguish it from other kanji containing the same radical, such as 「草」 (grass) and 「茶」 (tea), and from the component 「化」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q11-11.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「草」 means "grass" and is read 「くさ」 (kusa); below the grass radical is 早.
default.q.n5-type-1-q11-11.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「茶」 means tea and is read 「ちゃ」 (cha). It consists of the grass radical combined with 「人」 and 「木」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q11-11.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「化」 means “to transform” and is read 「か」(ka); it is missing the grass radical 「艹」at the top.
default.q.n5-type-1-q11-11.why.3: (d) Correct because 「花」 means “flower” and is read 「はな」 (hana). It consists of the grass radical 「艹」 on top and 化 below.
default.q.n5-type-1-q12-12.verdict: The correct answer is (b). 電気.
default.q.n5-type-1-q12-12.explanation: Meaning: “It’s dark in the room, so please turn on the light.” Key point: the kanji for 「でんき」 (electricity; electric light) is 電気. Do not confuse it with the similar-sounding word 「天気」 (weather - てんき), or with compounds containing 「電」 such as 「電車」 and 「電話」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q12-12.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「天気」means “weather” and is read 「てんき」(tenki), with the unvoiced sound て.
default.q.n5-type-1-q12-12.why.1: (b) Correct. 「電気」 means “electricity” or “electric light” and is correctly read 「でんき」 (denki).
default.q.n5-type-1-q12-12.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「電車」 means "train" and is read 「でんしゃ」 (densha).
default.q.n5-type-1-q12-12.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「電話」 means “telephone” and is read as 「でんわ」 (denwa).
default.q.n5-type-1-q13-13.verdict: The correct answer is (b). かさ.
default.q.n5-type-1-q13-13.explanation:
Translation: "Since it is raining outside, I will take an umbrella with me."
Key point: The everyday item noun 「かさ」(umbrella) is used with the weather-related expression 「雨（あめ）が ふる」(it rains).
default.q.n5-type-1-q13-13.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「かばん」 means “briefcase” or “bag,” not an item specifically used for protection from rain.
default.q.n5-type-1-q13-13.why.1: (b) Correct. 「かさ」 means “umbrella.” Since it is raining (雨が ふって います), the person needs to take an umbrella.
default.q.n5-type-1-q13-13.why.2: (c) Incorrect.「めがね」means “eyeglasses,” not something used to keep off the rain.
default.q.n5-type-1-q13-13.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「ぼうし」means “hat” or “cap,” not the main item used for going out in the rain in this context.
default.q.n5-type-1-q14-14.verdict: The correct answer is (d). とりました.
default.q.n5-type-1-q14-14.explanation:
Meaning: I took a lot of pictures during the trip.
Key point: The fixed N5 verb phrase 「写真（しゃしん）を とる」(take pictures).
default.q.n5-type-1-q14-14.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「かきました」, from 書く/描く, means “wrote/drew” and commonly goes with 「手紙（てがみ）を かく」 or 「絵（え）を かく」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q14-14.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「みました」(the verb 見る) means “watched” or “looked at,” not the act of taking a photograph during a trip.
default.q.n5-type-1-q14-14.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「よみました」(the verb 読む) means “read” and is commonly used with 「本（ほん）を よむ」(read a book) and 「新聞（しんぶん）を よむ」(read a newspaper).
default.q.n5-type-1-q14-14.why.3: (d) Correct. 「とりました」 (the verb 撮る) combines with 写真 to form the fixed expression 「写真（しゃしん）を とる」, meaning “to take a photograph.”
default.q.n5-type-1-q15-15.verdict: The correct answer is (a). ぜんぜん.
default.q.n5-type-1-q15-15.explanation:
Translation: This book is very difficult, so I do not understand it at all.
Key point: The adverb 「ぜんぜん」(not at all) is normally used with the negative form 「〜ません」to emphasize complete negation.
default.q.n5-type-1-q15-15.why.0: (a) Correct. 「ぜんぜん」 is an adverb used with the negative form 「〜ません」 to mean “not at all,” expressing that the book was so difficult that the speaker understood nothing.
default.q.n5-type-1-q15-15.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「いつも」means “always” and generally accompanies affirmative sentences describing habits; it does not fit the context of degree of understanding.
default.q.n5-type-1-q15-15.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「たくさん」means "many" or "a lot" and indicates quantity; it cannot be used with the negative 「わかりません」 to express a degree of understanding.
default.q.n5-type-1-q15-15.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「だんだん」means “gradually, little by little” and usually accompanies structures showing a change of state, such as 「〜になります」or「〜てきました」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q16-16.verdict: The correct answer is (c). 図書館（としょかん）.
default.q.n5-type-1-q16-16.explanation:
Translation: Because there is a book I want to read, I will go to the library to borrow it.
Knowledge point: The public-place noun 「図書館（としょかん）」 fits the purpose of borrowing a book, 「本（ほん）を かりる」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q16-16.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「病院（びょういん）」 means hospital, a place where illnesses are examined and treated.
default.q.n5-type-1-q16-16.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「銀行（ぎんこう）」 means "bank," a place where financial transactions are carried out.
default.q.n5-type-1-q16-16.why.2: (c) Correct. 「図書館（としょかん）」means “library,” a place where people go to read and borrow books (本を かります).
default.q.n5-type-1-q16-16.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「郵便局（ゆうびんきょく）」means “post office,” where letters and parcels are sent.
default.q.n5-type-1-q17-17.verdict: The correct answer is (b). くらく.
default.q.n5-type-1-q17-17.explanation:
Translation: Because I turned off the lights, the room became dark.
Key point: The i-adjective 「くらい」(dark) changes to the adverbial form 「くらく」when it modifies the verb of change 「なります」(to become).
default.q.n5-type-1-q17-17.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「あかるく」(the i-adjective あかるい, "bright") is the opposite of the result of turning off the lights.
default.q.n5-type-1-q17-17.why.1: (b) Correct. 「くらく」 is the form of the i-adjective くらい (dark). Turning off the light (電気を けす) makes the room become dark (くらく なりました).
default.q.n5-type-1-q17-17.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「ひろく」, from the i-adjective ひろい (“wide”), describes the area of a space and is unrelated to turning off the electricity.
default.q.n5-type-1-q17-17.why.3: (d) Incorrect.「せまく」(from the i-adjective せまい - narrow/cramped) describes the area of a space and does not change depending on whether the light is turned on or off.
default.q.n5-type-1-q18-18.verdict: The correct answer is (a). スプーン.
default.q.n5-type-1-q18-18.explanation:
Translation: Since I am going to have soup, please give me a spoon.
Key point: The katakana word for a table utensil, 「スプーン」(spoon), is appropriate for a liquid dish such as 「スープ」(soup).
default.q.n5-type-1-q18-18.why.0: (a) Correct. 「スプーン」(spoon) means “spoon” and is an utensil specifically used for eating or drinking soup (スープ).
default.q.n5-type-1-q18-18.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「フォーク」(fork) means "fork," used to spear stringy or solid foods such as noodles and meat.
default.q.n5-type-1-q18-18.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「ナイフ」(knife) means “table knife,” used for cutting hard or tough food.
default.q.n5-type-1-q18-18.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「コップ」(cup/glass) means a cup or glass used for holding drinks; it is not used for scooping and eating soup.
default.q.n5-type-1-q19-19.verdict: The correct answer is (b). この 本（ほん）は むずかしくないです。
default.q.n5-type-1-q19-19.explanation:
Question sentence translation: “This book is easy.”
Key point: At the N5 level, 「やさしい」 (easy) and the negative form of its antonym, 「むずかしくない」 (not difficult), express the same meaning.
default.q.n5-type-1-q19-19.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「長くない」（ながくない）means “not long,” describing the length or volume of a book; it is not synonymous with「やさしい」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q19-19.why.1: (b) Correct because the adjective 「やさしい」 means “easy” or “simple,” which is semantically equivalent to the negative form of its opposite adjective 「むずかしい」 (“difficult”): 「むずかしくない」 (“not difficult”).
default.q.n5-type-1-q19-19.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「おもしろくない」means “uninteresting” or “not enjoyable,” describing a book’s appeal.
default.q.n5-type-1-q19-19.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「安くない」（やすくない）means “not cheap” (expensive), describing price and having nothing to do with the difficulty or ease of a book.
default.q.n5-type-1-q20-20.verdict: The correct answer is (a). 田中（たなか）さんは 写真（しゃしん）を とる 仕事（しごと）を しています。
default.q.n5-type-1-q20-20.explanation:
Translation of the prompt: "Mr. Tanaka is a photographer."
Key point: In N5 Japanese, the occupation noun in katakana 「カメラマン」 (cameraman) can be converted into the corresponding explanatory phrase 「写真を とる 仕事」 (work involving taking photographs).
default.q.n5-type-1-q20-20.why.0: (a) Correct because the borrowed Katakana word 「カメラマン」(cameraman) means “photographer,” exactly matching 「写真を とる 仕事を しています」(works taking photographs).
default.q.n5-type-1-q20-20.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「えを かく 仕事」 means “work involving drawing pictures” (an artist / 画家), which does not match the occupation of a photographer.
default.q.n5-type-1-q20-20.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「車を 売る 仕事」means “a job selling cars” (a car salesperson), not a photographer.
default.q.n5-type-1-q20-20.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「料理を 作る 仕事」means “work involving cooking” (a cook / コック), not a photography profession.
default.q.n5-type-1-q21-21.verdict: The correct answer is (d). ゆうがた、雨が ふらなく なりました。
default.q.n5-type-1-q21-21.explanation:
Translation of the sentence: "By evening, the rain had stopped."
Key point: The weather-related N5 verb expression 「雨が やむ」 (the rain stops) corresponds to the change-of-state pattern 「〜なくなる / 〜なくなりました」 (to no longer be..., to stop...).
default.q.n5-type-1-q21-21.why.0: (a) is incorrect because 「ふりはじめました」 means “it began to rain,” describing the start of a weather event, which is opposite to the rain ending or stopping.
default.q.n5-type-1-q21-21.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「つよく なりました」 means “has become stronger” or “has intensified,” describing increasing rainfall rather than the rain stopping.
default.q.n5-type-1-q21-21.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「たくさん ふりました」means “it rained a lot,” referring to a large amount of rain in the past.
default.q.n5-type-1-q21-21.why.3: (d) Correct because the past form of 「やむ」(stop, cease), 「やみました」, expresses that the rain has stopped, equivalent to the change-of-state structure 「ふらなく なりました」(it no longer rains).
default.q.n5-type-1-q22-1.verdict: The correct answer is (a). 買い.
default.q.n5-type-1-q22-1.explanation: Translation: "Yesterday, I went to the store to buy bread." Key grammar point: The movement-purpose pattern 「V-ます (remove ます) + に 行きます/来ます/帰ります」 (go/come/return in order to do something).
default.q.n5-type-1-q22-1.why.0: (a) Correct. The purpose pattern for movement is 「verb ます-stem + に + 行きます/来ます」 (“go/come to do something”). Remove ます from 買います to get 買い.
default.q.n5-type-1-q22-1.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 買う is the dictionary form and cannot directly combine with 「に 行きました」 to express the purpose of going.
default.q.n5-type-1-q22-1.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 買って is the te-form, used to connect actions or with other patterns. It cannot directly precede 「に 行きました」to express purpose.
default.q.n5-type-1-q22-1.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Keeping the ます ending in 買います violates the required grammar; ます must be removed in this construction.
default.q.n5-type-1-q23-2.explanation: Sentence meaning: “I take the bus to school every morning.” Key point: the particle 「で」 indicates the means of transportation (バスで・電車で・自転車で).
default.q.n5-type-1-q23-2.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The particle 「に」indicates a destination or point in time; here, the destination is already marked by 「学校へ」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q23-2.why.1: (b) Correct. 「で」 follows a noun referring to a means of transportation to say that one travels by that means: バスで = by bus.
default.q.n5-type-1-q23-2.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「を」 marks the object of a transitive verb or a route with a movement verb (公園を歩く); it is not used for means of transportation.
default.q.n5-type-1-q23-2.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「が」 marks the subject; here the subject is the omitted speaker, not the bus.
default.q.n5-type-1-q24-3.verdict: The correct answer is (c). 食べて.
default.q.n5-type-1-q24-3.explanation: Meaning: 'You must not eat here.' Key grammar point: The prohibition or warning pattern 「V-て + は いけません」, meaning that someone must not do something.
default.q.n5-type-1-q24-3.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 食べ is the verb stem (the ます-form with ます removed), so it cannot combine with 「は いけません」 to form a prohibition pattern.
default.q.n5-type-1-q24-3.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 食べる is the dictionary form and cannot directly be combined with 「は いけません」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q24-3.why.2: (c) Correct. The standard pattern for prohibiting an action is 「verb te-form + は いけません」 (食べます → 食べて).
default.q.n5-type-1-q24-3.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 食べた is the short past form (た形), which is not used in this prohibitive rule pattern.
default.q.n5-type-1-q25-4.verdict: The correct answer is (d). 大きくて.
default.q.n5-type-1-q25-4.explanation: Translation: "Tanaka's house is big and new." Key grammar point: To connect two い-adjectives, change the ending to 「～くて」 to list similar characteristics.
default.q.n5-type-1-q25-4.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 大き is the stem formed by dropping the い ending from an i-adjective, so it cannot stand alone before another adjective.
default.q.n5-type-1-q25-4.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 大きいに is grammatically incorrect; an i-adjective does not take 「に」to connect to another adjective in this sentence.
default.q.n5-type-1-q25-4.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 大きいで incorrectly applies the linking ending 「で」used with na-adjectives and nouns to an i-adjective.
default.q.n5-type-1-q25-4.why.3: (d) Correct. When connecting two i-adjectives to list characteristics of the same type (both large and new), remove the final 「い」 and add 「くて」 (大きい → 大きくて).
default.q.n5-type-1-q26-5.verdict: The correct answer is (b). から.
default.q.n5-type-1-q26-5.explanation: Meaning: "The bank is open from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m." Key grammar point: The particle pair 「～から ～まで」 indicates a starting point and an ending point in time or space (from... to...).
default.q.n5-type-1-q26-5.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The particle 「まで」 marks an endpoint; inserting 「まで」 would repeat 「まで」 twice and make the time expression completely illogical.
default.q.n5-type-1-q26-5.why.1: (b) Correct. The particle pair 「～から ～まで」expresses “from one time point to another.” The particle after the starting point (9:00 a.m.) must be 「から」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q26-5.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The particle 「に」 indicates a specific point in time when an action occurs, so it does not combine with the endpoint 「～まで」 in this pattern describing a period of activity.
default.q.n5-type-1-q26-5.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The particle 「へ」 indicates the direction of movement in space; it is not used for a point in time.
default.q.n5-type-1-q27-6.explanation: Meaning: 'Of all the seasons, I like spring the best.' Key grammar point: the superlative pattern within a defined range: 「[Range] の 中で [Noun] が いちばん [Adjective] です」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q27-6.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The particle 「に」 indicates a time, destination, or recipient; it is not used to identify the item ranked “the best” in the comparison pattern 「〜の中で〜がいちばん〜」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q27-6.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The particle 「を」 marks the object of a transitive verb; 好き is a na-adjective expressing preference, so the liked object is not marked with 「を」 at the N5 level.
default.q.n5-type-1-q27-6.why.2: (c) Correct. In the superlative structure 「[range] の 中で [N] が いちばん [adjective] です」, the item being evaluated as “the most” always takes the particle 「が」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q27-6.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The particle 「で」 marks the scope of comparison (here, the scope is already expressed by 「1年の 中で」), so it does not come directly after the selected object.
default.q.n5-type-1-q28-7.explanation: Meaning: "Lee understands Japanese very well." Key grammar point: The verb expressing ability or a state of understanding, 「分かります」, takes the particle 「が」 to mark what is understood.
default.q.n5-type-1-q28-7.why.0: (a) Incorrect. Learners often mistakenly use 「を」out of habit from English grammar, but 分かります is a verb expressing a state or ability and does not take a direct object with 「を」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q28-7.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The particle 「に」 indicates a point in time, a place of existence, or a purpose/destination; it is not used as the complement of 分かります.
default.q.n5-type-1-q28-7.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The particle 「で」 indicates a means, tool, or place where an action occurs; it does not indicate the object of understanding.
default.q.n5-type-1-q28-7.why.3: (d) Correct. 分かります (to understand, know) is a verb expressing a state or cognitive ability, and the thing understood is marked with the particle 「が」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q29-8.verdict: The correct answer is (a). 行き.
default.q.n5-type-1-q29-8.explanation: Meaning: "I want to go mountain climbing with my friends next year." Grammar focus: The pattern expressing the speaker's own desire: 「V-ます (remove ます) + たいです」 (want to do V).
default.q.n5-type-1-q29-8.why.0: (a) Correct. The pattern expressing the speaker’s own desire is 「ます-form verb (remove ます) + たいです」. Remove ます from 行きます to get 行き.
default.q.n5-type-1-q29-8.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 行く is the dictionary form and cannot combine directly with the ending 「たいです」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q29-8.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 行って is the te-form and cannot combine with the auxiliary verb 「たい」, which expresses desire.
default.q.n5-type-1-q29-8.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 行か is the stem change of a Group 1 verb before the negative ending ない (nai-form), so it cannot combine with 「たい」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q30-9.explanation: Meaning: 'I watch movies three times a month.' Key grammar point: the pattern for expressing how often an action is performed during a period of time: 「[Period] に [Number of times] + V」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q30-9.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The particle 「で」 with a time expression indicates the time limit for completing something, meaning “within,” not a regular frequency or ratio.
default.q.n5-type-1-q30-9.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The particle 「を」 marks the object affected by a transitive verb (such as 映画を); it does not follow a phrase indicating a period of time.
default.q.n5-type-1-q30-9.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The particle 「は」 emphasizes or marks a topic and is not used in this standard expression of fixed frequency.
default.q.n5-type-1-q30-9.why.3: (d) Correct. The standard structure for expressing how many times an action is repeated within a period is 「[time period] + に + [number of times] + verb」, as in three times a month.
default.q.n5-type-1-q31-10.verdict: The correct answer is (c). お茶を.
default.q.n5-type-1-q31-10.explanation: The correct order is: 1 - 2 - 3 - 4. Complete sentence: 「わたしは まいあさ パンを 食べて、つめたい お茶を 飲んでから 学校へ 行きます。」 (Every morning, I eat bread, drink cold tea, and then go to school.) The key grammar point is using the te-form to connect a sequence of actions and the pattern 「〜てから」 to express doing one action before the next.
default.q.n5-type-1-q31-10.why.0: (a) is incorrect because 「食べて」 must come first, immediately after 「パンを」, to form 「パンを 食べて」 (eat bread), connecting to the following clause with the te-form.
default.q.n5-type-1-q31-10.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「つめたい」 is an i-adjective modifying the noun 「お茶」, so it must occupy the second position, immediately before 「お茶を」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q31-10.why.2: (c) Correct because 「お茶を」 occupies the third position (★) as the direct object of the verb 「飲んでから」 in the fourth position.
default.q.n5-type-1-q31-10.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「飲んでから」 (“after drinking”) must appear in the fourth position to connect with the following action 「学校へ 行きます」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q32-11.verdict: The correct answer is (a). 本を.
default.q.n5-type-1-q32-11.explanation: The correct order is: 2 - 4 - 1 - 3. Complete sentence: 「すみませんが、テーブルの 上に ある 本を 見せて ください。」 (Excuse me, please show me the book on the table.) Key grammar points: a relative clause modifying a noun (dictionary-form verb + noun: 「ある 本」) and the polite request pattern 「〜てください」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q32-11.why.0: (a) Correct, because 「本を」 is in the third position (the ★ position), is modified by the clause 「テーブルの 上に ある」, and functions as the object of 「見せて」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q32-11.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「上に」 must come first, immediately after 「テーブルの」, to form the location phrase 「テーブルの 上に」 (on the table).
default.q.n5-type-1-q32-11.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「見せて」must be placed fourth and directly combined with 「ください」at the end of the sentence to form the polite request 「見せて ください」(please show me).
default.q.n5-type-1-q32-11.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「ある」must appear in the second position, immediately after 「上に」, to form a modifying clause for the following noun.
default.q.n5-type-1-q33-12.verdict: The correct answer is (b). ひるごはんを.
default.q.n5-type-1-q33-12.explanation: The correct order is: 1 - 3 - 2 - 4. Complete sentence: 「いっしょに 駅の ちかくの 店へ ひるごはんを 食べに 行きませんか。」 (Would you like to go together to a restaurant near the station for lunch?). Key grammar point: the movement-purpose pattern 「Place + へ + verb stem (ます-form without ます) + に + 行きます」 combined with the polite invitation pattern 「〜ませんか」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q33-12.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「ちかくの」must come first, immediately after 「駅の」, to form the noun phrase 「駅の ちかくの」 (“near the station”).
default.q.n5-type-1-q33-12.why.1: (b) Correct because 「ひるごはんを」 occupies the third position (★) as the object directly accompanying the purpose expression 「食べに」 in the fourth position.
default.q.n5-type-1-q33-12.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「店へ」must be in the second position to receive the modifier 「ちかくの」and combine with the directional particle 「へ」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q33-12.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「食べに」must occupy the fourth position immediately before 「行きませんか」to complete the purpose-of-movement structure 「食べに 行きませんか」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q34-13.verdict: The correct answer is (d). うたう.
default.q.n5-type-1-q34-13.explanation: The correct order is: 1 - 2 - 4 - 3. Complete sentence: 「たなかさんは 日本の うたを とても 上手に うたう ことが できます。」 (Mr. Tanaka can sing Japanese songs very well.) Key grammar points: the ability pattern 「dictionary-form verb + ことが できます」 and the use of an adverb to modify a verb: 「na-adjective stem (remove な) + に + verb」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q34-13.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「とても」 means “very” and is an adverb of degree. It must come first to modify the following adverb 「上手に」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q34-13.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「上手に」(skillfully, well) is the adverbial form of the na-adjective 上手な and must appear in the second position to directly modify the verb 「うたう」.
default.q.n5-type-1-q34-13.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「ことが」must be in the fourth position, following the dictionary-form verb 「うたう」and combining with 「できます」at the end of the sentence.
default.q.n5-type-1-q34-13.why.3: (d) Correct because 「うたう」 is in the third position (★), is a verb in dictionary form following the complement 「上手に」, and comes before the nominalized expression 「ことが」.
